1. Prévo at a glance

Prévo is a CMMS (computerised maintenance management system) for a workshop or a small industrial site. It holds the equipment register, work requests, work orders, preventive maintenance, the spare parts stores, the planning, statutory inspections, the team and its authorisations, indicators and a monthly report.

  • Your data stays with you. It is 27 CSV files, readable in Excel, kept in a folder of your choice. The only connection Prévo opens to the Internet by itself is reading the public versions file once a day (2.9, can be switched off); added to that, only if you use them, are the online AI assistant (if the manager allows it) and voice dictation (the voice is transcribed by Google or Microsoft).
  • Nothing to install: Python comes in the zip. A double-click starts Prévo and its setup wizard, which sets up access for workstations and phones in three questions. To simply have a look, Chrome or Edge is enough (demo, folder mode).
  • In English or French, as each person chooses, and each screen adapts to the person's role: requester, technician or manager. Beyond the PC that hosts Prévo, each person has their own account and everything goes over https; requesters' phones are recognised by an invitation QR code, with no password.

The screenshots in this guide were taken on the demo data set: a fictitious workshop, the “Atelier des Trois Vallées”. No real person or company appears in it.

Back to contents

2. Getting started

Prévo installs in three steps: unzip, double-click, answer three questions. There is nothing else to install: Python comes in the zip. To simply have a look, the demo opens without installing anything (2.1).

Help on screen. The first time you open each screen, a box at the top of the page says what it contains and what you do there, and suggests something to try. It blocks nothing: Got it closes it for good on this workstation, Learn more opens the part of the guide that covers it, and the Esc key closes it for this time only. The Explanations link in the menu (the “i” icon at the top on a phone) reopens it at any time. To switch it off or see everything again: This workstation.

2.1 Try it without installing anything (30 seconds)

  1. Open the index.html file in the Prévo folder in Chrome or Edge (double-click it, or drag the file into the browser window).
  2. Click Try it with the demo data.
  3. Choose a profile. Manager sees everything.

A banner “Demo — nothing is saved” stays at the top of the screen: you can try anything, nothing is written to the disk. The demo dates are shifted to today. The Export as ZIP button lets you keep a copy of the demo data (27 CSV files). The online demo, on the Prévo website, is the same page: no accounts, no AI assistant.

On the start screen, the “Drop CSV files here” area opens your own CSV files in the same way: to look at them, without saving anything.

2.2 Folder mode: a single workstation, no server

  1. Create a folder for the data, for example Documents\Prévo-donnees.
  2. Open index.html in Chrome or Edge, then click Choose the data folder and pick that folder. The browser asks for permission to change it: accept.
  3. If the folder is empty, Prévo offers Start from the demo data (a complete fictitious workshop, which you can change) or Create an empty database (the CSV files with only their headers).
  4. Choose your profile and the name of this workstation.

The next times, Resume the previous folder saves you from choosing it again (the browser asks for permission again).

One workstation at a time. This mode is made for one PC, without phones; the AI assistant is set up there in “This workstation”, but Ollama refuses a page opened from the disk (see 5.6). If another session seems to be open on the same folder, Prévo says so (without blocking). To work with several people, with phones or with Ollama, install Prévo (2.3): even alone on one PC, that is the recommended mode. Firefox and Safari cannot open a folder: you need Chrome or Edge.

2.3 Installing Prévo (the server PC)

One PC runs Prévo: the “server PC”, or “workshop PC”. The other workstations and the phones connect to it with their browser. It can be your office PC, or better a small computer that stays switched on (mini-PC, Raspberry Pi, company server): Prévo can only be reached when that PC is on.

  1. Unzip Prévo into a folder of its own. On Windows, the recommended folder is C:\Prevo: short, stable, away from downloads and the desktop. If Prévo is somewhere else, the wizard will offer to move it there (each file is copied then checked; the old folder is never deleted).
  2. Double-click Lancer_GMAO.bat. The zip contains its own Python (the python folder): nothing to install, no questions. On Mac or Linux: ./lancer.sh (Python 3.11 or later).
  3. A black window opens and the PC's browser opens by itself on the setup wizard (2.4). Leave the window open: closing it stops Prévo. Once Prévo is set to start with the PC (8.7), there is no window at all any more.

Until the installation is finished, Prévo can only be reached from this PC: no other device can see it.

Did you have Prévo 1.2? Unzip version 2 into the old one's folder (the zip has no donnees folder: your files stay) and start it. The wizard sees your data (“Your Prévo 1.2 data is here: N files, last changed on …; it is kept”) and does not touch any CSV file: it only sets up access. The profiles remembered on the workstations are replaced by the accounts.

2.4 The setup wizard

The wizard asks three questions, then sets up the rest from your answers. Each step says who is affected, what it changes, why, and what Prévo recommends in your situation; “Set up another way” unfolds the fine settings (ports, accepted names, certificate files, session lengths…).

  1. Who will use Prévo? “Just me”, “A small team” or “I am the company's IT person”.
  2. Where must Prévo be reachable from? This PC only, the workshop Wi-Fi, or outside the workshop too. Beyond this PC, a password and https are compulsory: Prévo does not offer the opposite, because anyone on the same network could otherwise read the job reports or delete work orders.
  3. Your name and a password: the manager's account (at least 12 characters; a passphrase of several words is recommended). If you are alone on this PC: your name is enough, no password.

What Prévo then decides, from the situation you chose (everything can still be changed):

SituationReachable fromAccountshttps certificateStart-up, sleepSolo mode
Just meThis PC; or outside, through TailscaleNone on this PC; compulsory as soon as a phone is plannedThrough the private network, or automaticYour choice; sleep keptYes
A small teamThe workshop Wi-FiYes; requesters through an enrolled device (QR)Automatic, made by PrévoWith the PC; sleep preventedNo
IT personThe company network, behind a proxyYes, requesters includedYour own, or your proxy'sWith the PC, or your service toolNo

The following steps skip themselves when they do not apply: the certificate (8.3), Tailscale (8.6), starting with the PC (8.7), the folder where backups are copied (chapter 9), then the summary with the access record to print and keep near the PC. With no data to begin with, the summary asks what to start with: an empty database, or the fictitious demo workshop. Nothing is written before Finish: the wizard then writes prevo.config.json next to serveur.py, and Prévo restarts with these settings. Reloading or restarting before the end loses nothing: the wizard picks up where it left off.

Everything can be redone afterwards, from the server PC, in Settings › Access and installation; the IT person can also set everything in prevo.config.json or on the command line (serveur.py --aide lists every setting with its help). The access record can be reprinted from the same screen.

2.5 The three set-ups: Solo, Workshop, Intranet

Solo. One PC and, if needed, your phone. On this PC only: no accounts and no https; your name creates your technician record, and Prévo switches to Solo mode (8.8): a lighter menu, “New WO” first, closing in one step. For your phone, at home or on the move, Tailscale links the PC and the phone without opening the router (8.6); a password is then compulsory.

Workshop. A small team on the workshop Wi-Fi: the manager's account, then one account per technician (Team › Access, 8.2); requesters' phones enrolled with an invitation QR code, with no password; a certificate made by Prévo, which each phone recognises once (8.3); Prévo starts with the PC, which no longer goes to sleep. This is the set-up recommended for a workshop.

Intranet. The company's IT person installs Prévo on a server, behind the company's reverse proxy or VPN, with its own certificate; everyone, requesters included, has an account. After the first question, the wizard shows all the steps on one page, with nothing automatic. The details (configuration, nginx, Caddy and IIS proxies, Cloudflare Tunnel, services, accounts, log, backups) are in docs/INSTALLATION.md.

2.6 The Windows firewall

For workstations and phones to reach the server PC, Windows must let Prévo through. When Prévo starts with the PC (8.7), the installation script adds a “Prevo” rule to the firewall itself, limited to private networks and the workshop network. Otherwise, the first time it runs on the network, Windows asks whether to allow Python to communicate: tick only “Private networks”, never “Public networks”.

A phone cannot connect?

  • The PC's Wi-Fi network must be of the private type: Windows Settings, Network & internet, Wi-Fi (or Ethernet), network properties, “Network profile type”: Private network.
  • If you answered the firewall question too quickly: Control Panel, Windows Defender Firewall, “Allow an app or feature through Windows Defender Firewall”, Python: tick “Private”, untick “Public”.
  • The phone and the PC must be on the same Wi-Fi (a “guest” Wi-Fi often isolates the devices from each other).

2.7 Connecting a phone

  1. The phone must be on the same Wi-Fi as the server PC (or on the private Tailscale network, 8.6).
  2. On Prévo's home screen (manager), the “Connect a phone” card shows a QR code: scan it with the phone's camera, or type the address written on the access record.
  3. The first time, the phone shows the “Trust the workshop PC” page: it guides the installation of the workshop certificate, on Android and on iPhone, in a few screens (8.3). After that, Prévo opens over https, with the camera (scanning labels in Prévo) and the microphone (dictation).
  4. A technician or the manager signs in with their account (8.1). A requester does not need a password: the manager sends them an invitation (Team › Access, 8.2), the phone gives its name once and stays recognised for a year.

The QR labels stuck on the machines open the equipment record directly, with the “Report a problem” button. They contain the server PC's address: reserve a fixed address for this PC in the router, otherwise the labels lead nowhere the day the address changes.

2.8 Which mode should you choose?

ModeHow to start itWho it is forData
Demoindex.html, “Try it with the demo data”Discovering, presenting, trainingIn memory, nothing is saved (ZIP export possible)
Folderindex.html, “Choose the data folder”One PC only, Chrome or Edge (limited AI, 5.6)CSV files in the chosen folder
ServerLancer_GMAO.bat or lancer.sh, then the wizardOne PC alone (Solo mode), a team, phones, QR labels, the AI assistantCSV files in donnees on the server PC

2.9 Being told about new versions

Prévo does not update itself. To tell you about new versions, it reads the public file https://prevo.pro/version.json at most once a day per workstation, on the manager's workstation only. This check is on by default; it is switched off in Settings, “Updates” section, “Notify me of new Prévo versions” box. Until the manager has set it, a banner tells them once on their home screen (Got it removes it).

What is sent. Nothing but the request for the file: no ID, no installation number, no statistics, no cookie. As with any visit to a website, prevo.pro sees the workshop's public internet address, the browser's name and the address by which Prévo is opened on your network, which the browser adds by itself; its host may keep them in its logs. The only connection Prévo opens to the Internet by itself is this reading of version.json; added to it, only if you use them, are the online AI assistant and voice dictation.

If a newer version exists, a banner under the header of the manager's home screen says so, with its date and what is new: Download opens the version's page, Skip this version removes the banner until the next version. The “Update” line of the “About” screen gives the same status. Nothing installs by itself: you download the new version and put it in place yourself. The technician and the requester see nothing; if prevo.pro cannot be reached, nothing is shown; the online demo checks nothing.

3. Roles and profiles

Three roles, the same everywhere: requester, technician, manager. The role adapts the menu and the screens; with accounts, it is the server that checks it on every request.

RoleWhat they doScreens
RequesterReports a problem and follows their requests (they see the reason for a refusal or a postponement). Home, Report a problem, Requests, Equipment, Wiki, This workstation, About
TechnicianLinked to their team record: their work orders, carrying out the work, the job report, parts issued, technical closure. In addition: Work orders, Planning (view only), Preventive, Inspections, Stores, Team
ManagerEverything else: decisions on requests, preparation and scheduling, task lists, purchases, indicators, report, settings, accounts. All screens, including Indicators, Settings and Team › Access

With accounts (Prévo reachable beyond the server PC): the role comes from the account, not from a choice on screen, and the server refuses anything outside the role. A requester only reads the tables behind their screens (equipment, requests, failure codes, wiki pages; never costs, technicians or work orders), only adds requests and does not have the AI assistant. A technician sees neither the hourly rate nor prices, and changes neither the settings, nor the team, nor the suppliers. Backups, accounts, invitations and the sign-in log belong to the manager. A requester's phone enrolled by invitation has the requester's rights, under the name given at enrolment (8.2).

Without accounts (Prévo on this PC only, folder mode, demo): the first time it is opened, each workstation chooses a profile and a workstation name (written to the log with each change), as in Prévo 1.2.

A profile is not security. Without accounts, anyone can choose the Manager profile: profiles are there to simplify each person's screens. That is why Prévo refuses to listen on the network without accounts and https: away from this PC, there are only accounts.

To switch: with an account, “Sign out” at the bottom of the menu, then another person signs in; without an account, the This workstation screen, Change profile or workstation name… button (or the link under the profile, at the bottom of the menu). Solo mode (8.8) is not a fourth role: it is the manager, alone, with a lighter menu.

Back to contents

4. The screens, one by one

On a large screen, the menu is on the left (it folds away). On a phone, a bar at the bottom gives the main screens, and “More” gives the others.

4.1 Home

The home screen shows what needs attention, depending on the profile:

  • Manager: a summary sentence (“5 requests to handle, of which 1 safety”, then the overdue WOs, the open P1s and the week's preventive work), the “To handle first” item (the safety request or the oldest P1, otherwise the most overdue WO, otherwise the next preventive job), the counters “Requests to handle”, “Overdue WOs”, “open P1s” and “Preventive this week”, the requests to handle and the overdue work orders, then three tiles to keep an eye on: “Items to order”, “Inspections and authorisations”, “Preventive suggestions”. Each counter and each tile leads to the matching list. On a phone, the list of requests is in the bottom bar.
  • Technician: their open work orders.
  • Requester: their requests and what followed.

In server mode, the “Connect a phone” card shows the QR code for the PC's address. At the start of each month, the manager's home screen offers to finalise the report for the month just ended (Later to do it afterwards). As long as the database has no equipment, the manager's home screen offers Import data (see chapter 10).

4.2 Report a problem (work request)

Anyone can report a problem, including from a phone. Five questions:

  1. Which equipment? by searching (tag or name) or by scanning its QR label;
  2. What can you see? in a few words, with ready-made suggestions (leak, abnormal noise, vibration…);
  3. What is the impact? Safety (danger to a person), Stoppage (the machine no longer runs), Degraded (it runs, but badly), Disruption (can wait);
  4. Details (optional): since when, noise, smell, warning light…;
  5. A photo (optional): taken with the phone or chosen from the gallery.

Prévo calculates the priority as soon as the impact is chosen, from the equipment's criticality:

Equipment criticalityDisruptionDegradedStoppage
A (most critical)P2P1P1
BP3P2P1
C (least critical)P4P3P2

A Safety impact always gives P1, with a red banner. Default deadlines (adjustable): P1 immediate, P2 24 h, P3 7 days, P4 at the next stoppage.

4.3 Requests

The list of work requests and their status. The manager decides on each new request:

  • Accept: creates the work order;
  • Merge: attaches the request to a work order already open on the same equipment;
  • Defer: later, with a reason;
  • Decline: with a compulsory reason, which the requester sees.

On request and work order records, a “Common causes” box shows the most common causes of the same symptom on that equipment (or on equipment of the same make and model), from 5 cases up. It is a statistic from the history, not a diagnosis; below about twenty cases, Prévo adds “Few cases: treat it as a lead”.

4.4 Work orders

A work order (WO) goes through these stages: Created → Prepared → Scheduled → In progress → Technically closed → Administratively closed. It can also be On hold or Cancelled, always with a reason; a cancelled WO is never deleted. An emergency WO goes straight from Created to In progress.

A WO record has four tabs:

  • Preparation: work to be done, safety instructions, planned parts, technician, planned date, planned time;
  • Execution: checklist of tasks, time spent, parts issued and returned from the stores;
  • Job report: failure codes (symptom, cause, remedy), job report, “Tip for next time” (see 7.3), return to service;
  • Equipment history: past jobs on the same machine.

Rules applied by Prévo:

  • Moving to “Scheduled” is refused if a planned part is missing from stock: Prévo offers Put on hold (reason: part).
  • If the WO requires an authorisation, the assignment is refused when the chosen technician does not have it valid on the planned date (expired, missing or not yet obtained). The requirement comes from the equipment (“Authorisation required”) or from the WO (“Authorisation required by the work order”); a WO with no requirement is never blocked. Only the manager can Override and save: the “Required authorisation not valid” window asks for the box “I am overriding this on my own responsibility” to be ticked and for a reason to be written; the change log keeps who, when, which WO and which authorisation. A technician has no way to override. The same rule applies in the planning, on creation, on editing and when moving to “Scheduled”. When the equipment is under warranty, creating a corrective WO reminds you: “Call the supplier before any work?” (the reminder blocks nothing).
  • Technical closure requires: end date, time spent, cause code, remedy code, a job report of at least 10 characters (“NTR” is not accepted on a corrective job) and the “Equipment returned to service safely” box. The equipment's isolation procedure is shown on the WO: ticking a box does not isolate anything.
  • Administrative closure locks the WO and puts it in the wiki queue (see 7.4). To resume the work, you create a linked work order.
  • Cost of a WO = hours × hourly rate + parts issued × price + subcontracting.

Print the work order sheet gives a black-and-white A4 page. The list of WOs can be filtered, sorted and exported to CSV.

4.5 Planning

The week, Monday to Sunday: one row per technician, with their workload and capacity, and at the top the “Prepared” WOs to schedule, highest priority first. You drag a card onto a technician and a day, or use Schedule… (no mouse needed). The WO rules apply (missing part, required authorisation: the drag and drop is refused, with the same override for the manager). The technician views the planning; on a phone, it is shown as a list by day.

4.6 Preventive

A task list describes maintenance to be repeated regularly. It is triggered:

  • by a date (every 30 days, for example);
  • by a meter (every 2,000 running hours, for example);
  • by a measurement threshold (a temperature, wear…).

Each task list has its checklist of tasks, with the expected value where there is a measurement. When a technician or the manager opens Prévo, each overdue task list creates a single WO, with its checklist (even if two workstations open at the same time). Generate overdue WOs does it on demand. When the WO is closed, the task list restarts from the actual end date. Meter readings are entered on the equipment record. The “12-week calendar” tab shows the next 12 weeks (the number can be set in Settings).

If the technician sees a fault during a preventive job, one click on the WO opens a linked request and the WO is marked “fault found”.

4.7 Suggested preventive work

“Suggestions” tab of Preventive (manager). Prévo reads back through the history and proposes, with its rule, its figures, its dates and the WOs involved:

  • create a task list for equipment with no task list that has at least 3 breakdowns with the same cause in 12 months;
  • review the preventive maintenance of equipment that has at least 3 breakdowns with the same cause despite its task list;
  • review a task list whose visits often find a fault (2 of the last 4);
  • lengthen a task list where at least 5 visits in a row found nothing, with no breakdown at all (never for criticality A equipment; first check that no obligation requires it).

Prévo never changes a task list by itself and does not propose a new interval: Create the task list opens the pre-filled form, Open the task list takes you to the task list, Ignore… asks for a reason. Each decision is written to the log and listed in the “Decisions” tab; an ignored suggestion only comes back if new events reach the threshold. The “Understanding suggestions” box gives the definitions; the thresholds are set in Settings.

4.8 Stores

Tabs: Items, Movements, Stocktake (manager), Items to order, Purchases, Suppliers.

  • Stock is recalculated from the movements (receipt, issue, return, stocktake).
  • Every issue is charged to a WO; an issue that would make stock negative is refused.
  • Below the reorder point, the item moves to “Items to order”. Prévo suggests a value for the reorder point (consumption during the supply lead time + safety stock); you are the one who enters it.
  • A purchase request goes from “requested” to “ordered” then “received”; the goods receipt puts the stock in.

4.9 Equipment and QR labels

The tree of site, workshops, lines, and the record of each item of equipment: data sheet (tag, designation, make, model, criticality A, B or C, status, isolation procedure), QR code, meters and readings, preventive task lists, statutory inspections, sub-equipment, linked parts and job history. The manager adds and edits equipment.

Downtime cost per hour (manager): on the equipment record, what an hour of stopped machine costs (lost production, penalties, overtime…), in the currency set. Left empty, it reads “not costed”: Prévo never estimates this cost. The technician, the requester and the device do not see it. The record also shows “Under warranty until…” and the card of the equipment's warranties and contracts (see 4.12).

QR labels (manager): choose a workshop or a line (with everything it contains), an A4 sheet of 24 or 8 labels, and adjust the print offset if needed. The equipment tag is always written in plain text under the code. In folder and demo modes, the QR contains GMAO: followed by the ID, readable only by Prévo's scan on this workstation.

4.10 Statutory inspections

A schedule by equipment: overdue, findings to be cleared, to be scheduled (30 days or less), up to date. You record a completed inspection with its report (PDF or photo) and its findings, clear them one by one, and create a pre-filled statutory WO. Prévo calculates the next date from the inspection's interval; it does not monitor regulations.

Prévo is an aid to keeping track; responsibility remains with the employer.

  • Findings, line by line. When you record the inspection, the “Findings recorded” field takes one line per finding. Each finding has its own card, “Findings (n, m to be cleared)”, on the inspection record: its severity and due date if you entered them, Clear (date and what was done), Create a WO (pre-filled and linked to the finding), Add a finding for one that was missed, and “Show cleared findings” for the history. The inspection's status becomes “findings to be cleared (n)”. A new inspection deletes no finding: those that are not cleared stay open. With no due date entered, a finding is overdue 30 days after the inspection; overdue findings appear on the home screen and in the monthly report. Only the manager writes them.
  • From a 2.1 database. The free text “observations” of an existing inspection becomes one finding per non-empty line. An observation that was already cleared becomes a cleared finding with no invented date: its date stays empty, with the comment “cleared before 2.2, date unknown”.
  • The catalogue. When you create an inspection, Choose from the Prévo catalogue — French regulations pre-fills the type of inspection, the interval, the reference and the source type; Free entry (outside the catalogue) remains possible, and is the only option outside France. Each line says where its interval comes from: legal requirement (an article of the Labour Code, an order, a regulation), standard or recommendation, with the reference, the link to the text and the review date (“reviewed on…”). The lines that Prévo cannot vouch for carry the mention “to be confirmed with your inspection body” (shown in French, “à confirmer avec votre organisme de contrôle”), and the interval of some is for you to enter (for example according to your insurance contract). Everything can be edited; a value you change is marked “entered by hand” under “Origin”. The catalogue never changes an existing inspection: when it is reviewed, the record proposes the new values (Apply these values), and nothing changes without you. Its texts stay in French in every language.

4.11 Team and authorisations

The technicians (trade, capacity per week; the hourly rate is only visible to the manager) and their authorisations with their expiry date. A renewal adds a row and keeps the history. Authorisations that are overdue or expire within 60 days are flagged on the home screen. The Access button (manager, server mode) opens the accounts, the devices and the sign-in log (8.2).

Prévo is an aid to keeping track; responsibility remains with the employer.

  • The type, from the catalogue. Add an authorisation offers Type (Prévo catalogue — French regulations): electrical authorisations (NF C 18-510), CACES R482 to R490, operating authorisation… or Other (free entry). Choosing a type pre-fills the name and the refresher interval; the source type (legal requirement, standard or recommendation), the reference, the link and the review date are shown. The refresher interval for electrical authorisations is a recommendation, never presented as a requirement.
  • Refresher interval and expiry date. The technician's “Authorisations” card shows “Refresher interval: n months”. The expiry date is calculated from the date obtained plus the refresher interval; you can change it (date written on the certificate). With no refresher interval, the authorisation has no expiry date.
  • The supporting document. “Supporting document (PDF or photo)”, optional, 9 MB at most: certificate, attestation or CACES. In server mode with accounts, it is served only to the manager; the technician sees “supporting document attached, visible to the manager”.
  • The operating permit. It is issued by the employer: it is the one that is mandatory. The CACES is supporting evidence for it, not a replacement: choosing a CACES reminds you to also record the operating permit, which can reuse the CACES document.
  • The block. A WO that requires an authorisation cannot be assigned to a technician who does not have it valid on the planned date (see 4.4); only the manager can override, with the change log as evidence.
  • Who writes. In server mode with accounts, only the manager writes authorisations. The technician sees the “My authorisations” card (type, expiry date, valid or expired) on their home screen, without the supporting documents.

4.12 Warranties and contracts

Manager's screen (“Warranties” menu): equipment warranties and service contracts. Prévo reminds you of their due dates and keeps their documents; it sends nothing itself.

Prévo is an aid to keeping track; responsibility remains with the employer.

  • The list. Counters (“Current warranties”, “Ending within 60 days”, “Contracts: decision due”, “Dates to update”) that filter the list, then two tabs, Warranties and Contracts, with search and filters (supplier or contractor, status, “Under warranty today”, “Decision due or ending soon”). Each line gives its status and why. The total of current contracts is given per year; contracts with no amount are counted separately, never estimated.
  • A warranty. Equipment, supplier (optional, one from Stores), start, end, terms (what is covered, what voids it), attached certificate or invoice (PDF, JPEG or PNG). Statuses: not started yet, current, ending soon, ended, end date unknown.
  • A contract. Contractor (a supplier from Stores), subject, scope and equipment concerned (optional, the scope may be enough), start, end of the current period, termination notice in months, automatic renewal, optional annual amount excluding VAT in the currency set (the technician does not see it), signed contract attached. Prévo calculates the termination deadline (end minus notice).
  • The alerts. They come on 60 days before the end of a warranty, and before the termination deadline of a contract with automatic renewal, which becomes “decision due” (for example, ending on 31/12 with 3 months' notice: decision due from 01/08 to 30/09). A contract without automatic renewal, or whose termination has been recorded, is never “decision due”: it is “ending soon” before its end. Contract statuses: current, decision due, ending soon, notice deadline passed, dates to update, end date unknown, ended. The lead time is set in Settings › “Warranties and contracts” (“Alert before the due date (days)”, 60 by default, from 1 to 365). The manager's home screen has a “Warranties and contracts” tile.
  • The actions. On a contract: Write to the contractor (opens your email application, Prévo sends nothing), Record the termination (the date of the letter sent; the contract will no longer be renewed), Renew (a new period is proposed and can be edited). A contract with automatic renewal whose dates have passed must first be renewed before its termination is recorded. Remove on a warranty or a contract does not delete it: it is no longer shown or reminded and stays in the change log. Each record has its history.
  • On the equipment record. The “Under warranty until…” badge and the card of the machine's warranties and contracts, also visible to the technician (without amounts). Creating a corrective WO, or accepting a request, on equipment under warranty reminds you to call the supplier before any work.
  • Who writes. The manager only (refused otherwise). Contract documents are served only to the manager.

4.13 Indicators

Manager's screen: availability, MTBF (mean time between failures), MTTR (mean time to repair, with “of which waiting for parts” when the history allows), downtime, preventive share and compliance, overdue WOs, response times, maintenance cost and stock value. You choose the period (rolling 12 months by default), the criticality and the workshop.

  • Each figure says how many WOs it is based on and gives the list of its source WOs.
  • A figure that cannot be calculated says why, instead of showing zero.
  • Charts: Pareto of breakdowns and stoppages, hours per month (corrective and preventive), MTBF and MTTR of critical equipment, causes of breakdowns, technicians' workload and capacity; each with its values in a table and CSV and image exports.
  • The downtime cost: a “Downtime cost” Pareto (downtime × the downtime cost per hour on the equipment record) and the “Not costed” card, which lists the equipment with no hourly cost and the breakdowns with no duration, with the link “Enter the hourly cost”.
  • The “Understanding these indicators” box gives the definitions.

4.14 Monthly report

“Monthly reports” tab of Indicators. The report fits on one A4 page: key figures compared with the previous month and the previous year, highlights, and up to three points to examine, including “repair or replace?” when an item of equipment's maintenance cost over 12 months exceeds a threshold (50 % of its replacement value by default, adjustable).

The downtime cost has its “Downtime cost” tile (marked “Partial” when something is missing), its Pareto by cost in addition to the Pareto by hours, and its formula in “Understanding these indicators”: for the month's breakdowns, downtime × downtime cost per hour, rounded to the cent per item of equipment. Nothing is estimated: equipment with no hourly cost is listed as “not costed”, a WO with no duration is listed separately, and neither is counted. The report still fits on one A4 page. Manager only.

Finalise report saves it with the documents: it keeps the figures of the day and can be reopened without Prévo. Recalculate creates a new version of it. “Prepare an email” opens your email application with a summary: Prévo sends nothing itself. With the AI assistant, a comment can be proposed before finalising (see chapter 5).

4.15 Settings

Manager's screen:

  • Settings shared by all workstations: company name, deadlines by priority, priority of preventive WOs, tolerance for preventive compliance, “repair or replace” threshold, suggestion thresholds, authorisation of online AI providers (in server mode, the box shows the decision taken on the server PC, see 5.7), refresh frequency between workstations;
  • Warranties and contracts: “Alert before the due date (days)”, 60 by default (from 1 to 365), for warranties (before the end) and contracts (before the termination deadline);
  • Solo mode: switching to Solo mode or leaving it (see 8.8);
  • Access and installation (server mode, from the server PC): redo a step of the wizard, reprint the access record (see 2.4);
  • Updates: “Notify me of new Prévo versions” (see 2.9);
  • Failure codes (symptoms, causes, remedies): adding and renaming;
  • Backups and restoring (see chapter 9);
  • Database check: broken references, duplicates, values in the wrong format;
  • Import data: bring in your lists and your history from Excel, OpenDocument or CSV (see chapter 10);
  • Export as ZIP: the 27 CSV files and the attached documents.

4.16 This workstation

A screen open to all profiles. Its settings apply only to this browser: they change nothing on the other workstations (except the language chosen “for my account”, below).

  • Identity: workstation name, profile, storage, and Change profile or workstation name…;
  • AI assistant: on or off, model, response time-out, Test the connection, and where the texts go. In server mode, the provider, its address and its key are set on the server PC and only displayed here; in folder mode, they are entered on this workstation (see chapter 5);
  • Voice dictation: offer it or not on this workstation, and the detected status (see chapter 6);
  • Display: dark theme (the default) or light, for a bright room or full daylight. Printing stays black on white. Screen language: with an account (server mode, accounts required), two choices: “For my account”, the language is saved in your account and follows you to every workstation you sign in on; “For this workstation only”, it stays in this browser (and your account no longer imposes its own). On signing out, the screen goes back to the workstation's or the installation's language, for the next person. Without an account, the language applies to this workstation;
  • Screen help: the “Show the explanation on the first visit to each screen” box (ticked by default) and See all the explanations again, which brings them back once on each screen.

The “About” screen gives the version, the storage modes, the licences of the bundled libraries and the security limits.

The “Suggest an improvement” link (in “About” and at the bottom of the menu, for all profiles) opens GitHub in a new tab, on a form already filled in with only Prévo's version, the language and your browser (name, version, system, for example “Chrome 130, Windows”). Nothing is sent before your click, no data from your workshop, no name or account; you read and edit everything before sending, and you need a GitHub account. Without an account: the “by email” link writes to contact@prevo.pro with the same content.

Back to contents

5. The AI assistant

The AI assistant is optional and switched off by default. Without it, Prévo works in exactly the same way and calls no service. It is switched on workstation by workstation, in “This workstation”. In server mode, the provider (Ollama on the workshop PC, or an online service) is set once on the server PC, and the server passes the requests from all workstations and phones to it: no key travels over the network. With accounts, the AI assistant is reserved for technicians and the manager: a requester (an account or an enrolled phone) does not see “Suggest with AI” and the server refuses to relay their requests.

5.1 The AI suggests, you validate

  • Each suggestion appears in a box headed “AI proposal — provider, model”, with Use, Edit or Ignore.
  • The AI never fills in a field on its own, never changes a status and never saves anything: your usual save does the writing. The one exception is the checklist of a task list: the ticked tasks are added when you click Add the ticked tasks.
  • When a field filled in by the AI is saved, the log says so (“AI suggestion used”, with the name of the model).
  • An AI can make mistakes: always read the suggestion carefully.

5.2 What the AI can do

WhereButtonWhat you get
Report a problem (technician and manager, with accounts)Suggest with AIA clear symptom and an impact suggested from your text. If you have chosen “Safety”, the AI cannot lower that impact.
WO, Job report tabWrite the job reportYour loose notes become a structured job report: finding, cause, action, parts, work still to do. Cancel the suggestion gives back the original text as long as nothing has been saved.
WO, Job report tabSuggest codesSymptom, cause and remedy chosen only from your failure codes. A code invented by the AI is reported and ignored.
Task list record (manager)Suggest a checklistStarting tasks, to tick before adding them.
Import data (manager)Suggest with AIA field for each column that Prévo did not recognise, based on its title alone; the suggestion stays “to confirm” (see 10.4).
Wiki log (manager)Process the queueFor each administratively closed WO, short texts for the wiki pages: checked by Prévo, then validated by you (see chapter 7).
Monthly reports (manager)Suggest a commentA comment on the month. Prévo copies the figures into it: a figure written by the AI itself causes the suggestion to be refused. The finalised report carries the note “Comment written with the help of AI, reviewed and validated by the manager”.

With dictation: dictate your notes into the job report, then Write the job report.

5.3 What is sent to the AI

Only what each function needs:

  • request: the symptom and description entered, the tag and designation of the equipment, the list of impacts;
  • job report: the text of the field, the title and type of the WO, the tag and designation of the equipment, the parts issued (designation and quantity);
  • codes: the job report, the title of the WO, the symptom of the original request and your three lists of codes;
  • checklist: the designation, make and model of the equipment; the label, trigger and interval of the task list; the targeted cause if the task list comes from a suggestion;
  • summary: the last 20 WOs of the equipment (date, type, title, codes, start of the job report);
  • report comment: the month, its figures and its points to review;
  • import: the titles of the unrecognised columns and the list of possible fields, never the contents of the cells.

Never sent: the names of technicians and requesters, hourly rates, WO costs, documents and photos. Be careful: a text that you typed is sent as it stands; if it contains a name, that name is sent too.

5.4 Installing Ollama (AI on a workshop PC)

Ollama is free software that runs an AI model on a PC, without the internet once the model has been downloaded. It is Prévo’s default provider.

  1. Download and install Ollama from its official website, https://ollama.com (Windows, Mac or Linux).
  2. Download the recommended model: open a command prompt and type 
    ollama pull qwen2.5:7b
    (about 4.7 GB to download, once only).
  3. Ollama then answers at the address http://localhost:11434, which is the one Prévo suggests by default.

In server mode, install Ollama on the workshop PC (the one that runs Prévo): all workstations and phones go through the Prévo server, which passes the requests to Ollama. The address of the provider is that of the server PC (ia_url, http://localhost:11434 by default, where localhost means the workshop PC): no other setting is needed.

5.5 The recommended model: qwen2.5:7b

Prévo recommends the qwen2.5:7b model, the one chosen in the specification. It has been tested on the development PC with a set of test cases in French (rewording a request, job report, choosing codes from a closed list).

Measurements from 21/10/2026 on that PC (RTX 3060 6 GB graphics card, 16 GB of memory), in server mode, on the demo data set:

FunctionResultResponse time
Failure codes (12 real WOs from the demo)32 correct codes out of 36 (89 %): symptom 11/12, cause 11/12, remedy 10/12; no invented code (closed list)8.6 s median (22 s for the very first request: Ollama loads the model)
Rewording a request (4 work requests)clear symptom and suggested impact for each oneabout 9 s
Job report from brief notes (4 WOs)structured text (finding, cause, action, parts, work still to do); “not specified” when the notes say nothingabout 16 s

The errors seen are neighbouring choices (remedy “cleaning” instead of “adjustment”, “Other” codes for a fault that could not be reproduced replaced by precise codes) and a “Safety” impact suggested for a compressor that “went into safety” (a protective shutdown of the machine): always read the suggestion before using it. The test can be run again with tests/test_ia_reel.py (variable PREVO_TEST_IA=1).

Speed depends mainly on the PC’s graphics card: without a graphics card, a response can take more than a minute. The timeout is set in “This workstation” (120 seconds by default, 300 at most). Another model installed in Ollama can be chosen: Test the connection lists the available models.

5.6 Switching on the AI on a workstation

  1. Open This workstation, “AI assistant” card.
  2. Tick “Enable the AI assistant on this workstation”. Model: qwen2.5:7b. In server mode, the provider and its address are those of the server PC (shown, with no field); in folder mode, the provider is Ollama and the address is http://localhost:11434.
  3. Test the connection: “Connection successful” and the list of models found.
  4. Save. The AI buttons appear on the screens, and a permanent note says where the texts go (“AI: stays on this PC”…).

Prévo checks once only, on opening, that the provider is responding. If it does not respond, the AI buttons do not appear and the note adds “not responding”: Prévo works as it does without AI.

Ollama on another workshop PC: on that PC, set the OLLAMA_HOST variable to 0.0.0.0 so that Ollama listens on the network (see the Ollama documentation), and enter its address in the configuration of the server PC, for example http://192.168.1.30:11434.

Folder and demo modes: Ollama refuses the page. Prévo’s page is then opened from the disk (its address starts with file://) and the browser calls the provider itself (set in “This workstation”). Ollama refuses these calls by default (message “Ollama is refusing this page (403)”), and this guide no longer recommends the setting that would open Ollama to any web page open on that PC (a finding of the security audit). For the AI, run Prévo in server mode, even if you are alone on that PC (2.3): the relay goes through the server PC. In folder mode, the key of an online service stays in this browser (“This workstation” shows it); server mode keeps it on the server PC.

5.7 Online providers (OpenAI, Mistral, Groq…)

Prévo can also talk to any “OpenAI-compatible API”: an online service, or LM Studio on a PC (http://localhost:1234/v1). An online service sends the texts outside the workshop, to that provider. This is a company decision, so:

  1. The manager first allows it for the whole workshop. In server mode, the decision is made on the server PC (setting ia_en_ligne: the installation assistant under “Set up another way”, Settings › Access and installation, or prevo.config.json); the “Allow online AI providers” box in Settings shows it without changing it. In folder mode, that box decides. By default it is not allowed; without this permission, a workstation that tries receives “The manager has not allowed online providers”. The local AI (Ollama) is always still possible.
  2. Then the provider: “OpenAI-compatible API”, base address (often ending in /v1, for example https://api.mistral.ai/v1) and the access key supplied by the service. In server mode, they are set once on the server PC (ia_fournisseur, ia_url, ia_cle, or the environment variable PREVO_IA_CLE; never on a phone); in folder mode, in “This workstation”. Each workstation then chooses the model and switches on the assistant.
  3. When you save, Prévo warns you: “The texts sent — descriptions, job reports, designations — go to …; they may contain names.” You have to confirm (Enable anyway).

The access key is never shown again or written to the log. In server mode, it stays on the server PC: the server presents it to the provider and never sends it to browsers. In folder mode, it stays in the browser of that workstation.

Some online services refuse calls that come directly from a browser: in folder and demo modes, Prévo then says “The AI provider is not responding to this browser (…): use server mode”. Server mode does not have this problem: it is the Prévo server that calls the service.

5.8 Where do the texts go?

When the AI is active, a text note stays displayed in Prévo:

NoteWhen
AI: stays on this PCFolder and demo modes, provider on this PC (localhost).
AI: stays on the workshop PCServer mode, provider on the PC that runs Prévo.
AI: stays in the workshopProvider on another PC of the local network (address in 192.168…, 10…, 172.16 to 172.31…, or a name ending in .local).
AI: data sent to service nameAny other address: an online service.

5.9 If the AI does not respond

MessageWhat to do
Ollama is not responding (localhost)…Check that Ollama is running (icon near the clock), on the workshop PC in server mode.
Ollama is refusing this page (403)…Page opened without a server (folder and demo modes): run Prévo in server mode (5.6).
Connection successful…, but the model “…” is not in the list.Download it (ollama pull qwen2.5:7b) or choose a model from the list.
The AI did not respond within … s (workstation timeout).Try again, or increase the timeout in “This workstation”.
The workshop PC cannot reach the AI provider…Server mode: Ollama must be running on the workshop PC.
The AI provider is denying access (401)…Check the access key of the online service.
The AI provider is not responding to this browser (…): use server modeOnline service in folder and demo modes: run Prévo in server mode (see 5.7).
The manager has not allowed online providers…See 5.7, or use Ollama.
Back to contents

6. Voice dictation

A Dictate button (a microphone) sits next to the long text fields: details of a request, job report, reasons, report comment. Click, speak, then click again to stop. The recognised text is added to the end of the field: nothing that was already written is erased. You can correct it before saving.

Where does the voice go? In Chrome and Edge, the voice is sent to Google or Microsoft servers to be transcribed. Prévo says so the first time you use it on each workstation, with two choices: Continue or Turn off dictation. If the browser can transcribe French on the device itself, Prévo detects this and says so instead (“Your voice is transcribed on this PC”). In “This workstation”, the “Where is the voice transcribed?” button asks the browser the question.

  • Turning it off on a workstation: “This workstation”, “Voice dictation” card, untick “Offer dictation on this workstation”.
  • Browser without speech recognition (Firefox, for example): no button.
  • The microphone is allowed only on a secure page: on the PC itself (page opened from the disk, or http://localhost) or over https. On another workstation using http://192.168…, there is no button.
  • On a phone without https, Prévo shows “Dictation: use the microphone on your phone’s keyboard.” instead. The phone’s keyboard (Gboard on Android, the iPhone keyboard) has its own microphone: tap the field, then the keyboard’s microphone.
  • Possible messages: “Microphone blocked: allow the microphone for this page”, “No microphone found”, “Dictation not possible: no connection to the recognition service”.
Back to contents

7. The maintenance wiki

The maintenance wiki is the workshop’s encyclopaedia: one page for each machine, breakdown, stores item, technician, job and piece of know-how, all linked to one another. It opens from the Wiki menu. Prévo itself writes in it everything that can be calculated from the data (breakdowns, jobs, parts, stock); the AI assistant, if switched on, also suggests short texts drawn from closed work orders, which the manager validates. Without AI, the wiki still exists: it shows the facts, without the written texts.

7.1 What it is for and what you find in it

Before starting a job, a technician opens the machine’s page: there they see its isolation procedure at the top, its most frequent breakdowns, its latest jobs, the parts fitted and used, the know-how that applies to it and, in a few sentences, what the workshop has learned about it (“In brief”, “Tips”). Every name is a link to another page.

The wiki home page can be read in one sentence, “What the workshop knows”: so many machines, breakdowns, items, technicians and pieces of know-how, drawn from so many closed jobs; each number leads to its list. Below it: the search field, the five blocks (Machines, Breakdowns, Items, Technicians, Know-how), the latest jobs and the most frequent breakdowns. The manager also has “Wiki tracking”: suggestions to validate, contradictions to settle, failed WOs, the Process the queue button and the link to the wiki log.

Two layers, always kept separate:

  • The facts, calculated by Prévo without AI each time a page is displayed: record, breakdowns, jobs, parts, stock, authorisations. They are not written anywhere and cannot be wrong with respect to the data.
  • The written texts, short and dated: each sentence cites at least one WO, shown by a small number that leads to the job (the page ends with the “References” list). A banner states their origin: “Written with the AI (model) from the cited WOs — validated by … on …” or “Written by … on …”. Never any safety instruction in these texts: safety stays in the machine’s isolation procedure, shown at the top of its page and of its know-how pages.

7.2 The six types of page and who sees what

PageWhat Prévo calculatesWhat the AI writes
MachineRecord (tag, location, make, serial number, criticality, status, authorisation, sub-assemblies), isolation procedure at the top, frequent breakdowns, jobs, items fitted and used, know-how, task lists and inspections.“In brief” (3 sentences and 60 words at most, rewritten in full after each job) and “Tips” (10 sentences at most).
Breakdown (a symptom code)Machines affected, causes and remedies met, items changed, jobs, first and last case.Nothing.
ItemRecord (reference, manufacturer, bin location, stock, thresholds, supplier, price), stock over time (orders, issues with their WO, stock-outs), where it is fitted, what it was used on, jobs where it was used.“What it is for” (3 sentences and 80 words at most): its role and its signs of wear, as the WOs describe them.
TechnicianTrade, capacity, hours logged, authorisations and their status, jobs, hourly rate.Nothing: the name is never sent to the AI.
Job (a WO)The whole WO, read-only: machine, technicians, dates, stoppage, breakdown, cause, remedy, original request, work, job report, tip, parts, tasks, time; “Cited in the wiki”; Open the WO record to edit.Nothing.
Know-howThe machines where it is used (with the link to their isolation procedure), the linked items.All the text: “When to do it”, “Steps”, “Parts and tools”, “Pitfalls”, “Machine-specific details” (30 sentences and 600 words at most, sub-pages beyond that). Only one piece of know-how per task, shared by the machines.

In every list of jobs, open WOs come first (those in progress at the top), then the others from the most recent to the oldest, each with its status.

Who sees what. The wiki is open to all three profiles, with some differences:

  • Manager: everything, and only the manager sees the pending suggestions, the log, the queue and the hourly rate of technicians.
  • Technician: everything except the hourly rate.
  • Requester: machines, breakdowns, items (without prices) and know-how; no Technician page (the name stays without a link) and no Job page (the WO number stays without a link, and the small number only shows its tooltip).

From an equipment record, the “Wiki for this equipment” link opens its page; from an item record, “Wiki for this item”.

7.3 The tip at closure

In the Job report tab of a WO, below the job report, the “Tip for next time” field takes one short sentence: what would have saved you time (500 characters at most). It is optional, never required to close, editable until administrative closure, shown on the closed WO and on its Job page, and found by the search. It is the first source of know-how: the AI uses it before the job report. Safety instructions have no place in it; they stay in the equipment’s isolation procedure.

7.4 The queue and “Process the queue”

A WO’s entry into the wiki is called ingestion. It happens in two steps:

  1. At administrative closure, the WO enters the wiki queue (message “WO added to the wiki queue”). Nothing else happens: no request is sent.
  2. The manager processes the queue whenever they like: “Wiki tracking”, on the wiki home page, leads to the “Queue” view of the log, where the Process the queue button is found. It appears only on a workstation where the AI assistant is switched on (chapter 5); elsewhere, and in the online demo, a message says so in its place. Prévo sends one fresh request per WO, from the oldest to the most recent by job date, up to five at once when they touch no common page; progress is displayed, and Stop lets the requests already sent finish without starting any others. You can leave the screen: the summary is waiting when you come back.

What is sent (see also 5.3): the WO (title, work, symptom, cause, remedy, job report, tip, parts issued, downtime, symptom of the original request), the tag, the designation, the make and the model of the machine, the current text of the pages concerned (its machine, the items used, the linked know-how; eight at most) and the catalogue of titles for links. Never the names of technicians or requesters, costs, documents or photos.

What a WO costs. With an online provider, each WO is one request. Measured on the demo with Claude Sonnet (model claude-sonnet-5-5): 227 WOs ingested for $5.16, that is $0.026 per WO (about 2.5 cents); out of 242 responses, 15 were refused by the checks and then corrected on the second attempt. This figure depends on the provider, the model and the length of the job reports. With Ollama in the workshop, nothing is charged; it is slower, and the result has not been measured.

What Prévo checks before a response becomes a suggestion:

  • each sentence cites at least one WO, either the one being ingested or a WO already cited on the page; no other page counts as evidence;
  • no number that is not in the WO or in the text already written on the page; no count (“three times”), no frequency (“often”), no date: Prévo already calculates all of that;
  • no word from the safety vocabulary (isolation, padlock, de-energised, PPE…);
  • the length of each heading, at most three pieces of know-how created per WO, only one piece of know-how per task (a title too close to an existing title is refused), links to pages that exist;
  • nothing is removed from an existing page (sentences and cited WOs stay, except in “In brief”, rewritten in full); anything that contradicts a sentence goes into the contradictions, not in its place;
  • for a WO older than facts already ingested (“previous job”), no sentence presents its information as the most recent.

A refused response is requested again once, automatically, with the reasons for the refusal. If refused again, the WO is “failed” with its reasons: the manager can run it again later. The AI can also answer “nothing to add” (a preventive WO with no remarks, for example): this is recorded in the log, nothing is suggested.

WOs closed before the wiki existed or imported from another CMMS are not in the queue. The “Not in the wiki” view of the log counts them and offers to Add them, all of them or by equipment, after you have seen how many there are.

7.5 The log: validate, reject, run again

The wiki log (manager) has seven views: Log, To be validated, Contradictions, Queue, Failed, Not in the wiki, Wiki check. A suggestion shows the WO, its job date, the model that answered and, page by page, what changes: new sentences highlighted, reworded sentences with the old form struck through, identical sentences folded away, pages created in full.

  • Validate applies the suggestion as a whole. The tick boxes and Validate the selected proposals validate several at once; a suggestion that carries a contradiction is validated on its own.
  • Reject asks for a reason. The following suggestions that touch the same pages go back to “to be redone”: their WO returns to the queue and will be processed again on the new state.
  • Run again puts a failed or rejected WO back in the queue.

Suggestions are chained: each is built on the validated state plus those still waiting. You can therefore have ten WOs processed, then review them. As long as a suggestion is not validated, the other profiles see only the validated state.

Wiki check: the last view of the log re-reads the whole wiki without AI: broken links, orphan pages, pages with no WO cited, titles too close together, texts that are too long, contradictions open for more than 30 days, pages anchored on equipment or an item that has been removed. Nothing is corrected automatically: each line leads to the page.

7.6 Contradictions

When a WO contradicts a sentence that has already been validated (the seal was not at fault, it was the coupling), the AI does not correct the sentence: it reports the contradiction. The page then shows a “To be settled” box at the top, visible to everyone, with what the page says, what the WO observed and its number. The manager settles it from the page, with an optional note:

  • Keep the old one: the sentence does not change;
  • Replace with the new one: Prévo opens the page’s manual editor so that you can correct the sentence (see 7.7);
  • Both are true: both observations stay.

The decision is recorded in the log. A contradiction coming from a WO older than the facts on the page is presented as an earlier observation.

7.7 Writing by hand

The manager can write without AI, or correct what it has written: Edit on the page of a machine, an item or a piece of know-how; Write a know-how page on the page of a machine or an item (this is the only page that gets created: the others always exist). The text is written in simple markup, which the screen’s help reminds you of: a line ## Heading, then one line - sentence [OT-2026-0012] per sentence, a link to another page in double square brackets ([[PO-02 — Pompe centrifuge]]). Save applies the same checks as for the AI (citations, numbers, safety, lengths): a refusal shows its reasons and writes nothing. Archive removes a page after confirmation. AI suggestions that were waiting on that page go back to “to be redone”.

7.8 Search

The wiki search does not use AI and makes no network call. From the wiki home page, it first finds pages by name (machines, breakdowns, items, technicians depending on the profile, know-how), then closed jobs (title, job report, tip, codes) and wiki texts, with a highlighted extract. The same engine serves the “Search the history” field in the Preparation tab of a WO: it searches the WO’s machine first, then those of the same make and model, then the rest of the equipment register. On a work request, the “Seen before on this machine?” panel does the same search from the symptom entered.

7.9 The demo wiki

The wiki in the demo data set was built as it would be at a customer’s site: the 227 administratively closed WOs in the demo were put in the queue and processed by Claude Sonnet with Prévo’s instructions, a fresh agent per WO, in the order of the jobs, then validated in the name of the fictional manager (two recent suggestions are left “to be validated”, to show the screen). Result: 42 texts, that is 26 machines, 12 items and 4 pieces of know-how, and 90 WOs with “nothing to add”. The “About” screen mentions this. These texts were reviewed, but they come from an AI: they describe a fictional workshop. The demo itself calls no AI: its queue is empty and no request is sent. To try out ingestion, close a demo WO administratively on a workstation where an assistant is set up in “This workstation” (in demo mode, without a server, Ollama refuses the page: see 5.6), then Process the queue.

Back to contents

8. Access and installation

This chapter goes into detail on what the assistant (2.4) set up in a few clicks: accounts, trust for phones, access from outside, starting with the PC, Solo mode, and what all this changes for your data.

8.1 Signing in

With accounts, everyone signs in with their username (in the form prenom.nom, given by the manager) and their password. The workstation name is no longer asked for: the log records the account.

  • First sign-in. The manager gave you a temporary password (created with your account, shown only once). Prévo makes you change it before anything else: at least 12 characters, 256 at most, no composition rules; a passphrase of several words is recommended, and Prévo tells you as you type whether it is too short, acceptable or strong.
  • “Stay signed in on this device”. If ticked, the session lasts 30 days on this phone or workstation; otherwise 12 hours without activity, after which Prévo asks for the password again. Both durations (session, and “stay signed in”) are set in Settings › Access and installation.
  • Session ended while you were typing. Prévo shows the sign-in screen without erasing anything: when you sign in again with the same account, you find the screen as you left it, with what you had typed, and it is still to be saved. If someone else signs in on this workstation, they are not shown what you had typed.
  • Drafts. The report of a problem and the job report of a WO are kept as you type in the device’s browser, for your account only: if the phone goes to sleep and the page reloads, they come back with the “Draft restored” banner. Nothing is sent to the server before you save; the draft is deleted when you save, or after 7 days (the photo of a report is not kept in it).
  • Wrong password. The message is the same whatever the case (“Incorrect username or password”). From the fifth failed attempt in a row, Prévo makes you wait a few seconds; at the tenth, the account is locked for 15 minutes, and the screen shows the time remaining.
  • Signing out: at the bottom of the menu. A password that has been changed or reset closes all the other sessions of the account; a deactivated account (Team › Access) loses its sessions immediately.
  • Forgotten password. No email is sent: Prévo does not have your address and never sends anything. On the server PC, the manager double-clicks Reinitialiser_mot_de_passe.bat, types the username, and a temporary password is shown once only, to be changed at the first sign-in. From Team › Access, Reset… does the same for another account. Whoever has control of the server PC has control of Prévo: keep it somewhere safe.

8.2 Accounts and devices: Team › Access

Manager screen, Access button on the Team screen (server mode, accounts required). Three tabs:

  • Accounts: Create an account (first name, surname, role; a technician is linked to their record in the team; the person’s language, “Installation language” by default, which they can also choose themselves in This workstation), then on each row Edit…, Reset… (new temporary password), Deactivate or Activate. The temporary password is shown once only, in a window: note it down for the person, it is not written anywhere. There is always at least one active manager, and a deactivated account loses its sessions immediately.
  • Devices: Invite a device gives a QR code and a link valid for 1 hour to 7 days. The phone that opens it enters its name, then stays recognised for a year without a password, with the rights of a requester. The list shows each device (person, phone, last activity): Revoke cuts it off from its next request, and it sees the invitation page again. If every requester has an account (an IT administrator setting), enrolling devices is turned off.
  • Sign-in log: who signed in, when, from which address, with which browser; failures, lockouts, invitations, revocations, accounts created, edited or reset, and language changes (“Language changed (fr → en)”). The log is kept for 12 months and can be exported as CSV (see 8.9).

8.3 Trusting the workshop PC

Away from the server PC, Prévo talks over https: the connection is encrypted, the password does not travel in clear over the Wi-Fi, and the phone’s browser allows the camera (scanning labels in Prévo) and the microphone (dictation). To make this work, the server PC presents a workshop certificate, which Prévo makes itself (with the mkcert tool, supplied in the zip) for the PC’s address and name. This certificate is not signed by an authority known to phones, because the workshop is not on the internet: each phone therefore has to recognise it once. Two minutes, guided by Prévo, once per phone.

All the addresses that Prévo gives out (home page QR, labels, access record) are those of the front door, over http (for example http://192.168.1.20:8080); the https address is never something you type. A phone that scans a label or the home page QR arrives at this door: if it already trusts the workshop PC, Prévo opens straight away over https, on the requested record; otherwise, the “Trust the workshop PC” page is shown, recognises Android or iPhone, and guides you step by step, with one numbered step per phone screen, an illustration and a Try again button. Never a browser error. The access record also carries a “Trust the workshop PC” QR that leads to this page.

The certificate is only used to recognise the workshop PC: it gives no access to the phone and can be removed at any time in the same settings. Printed labels do not change address. If the address or the name of the PC changes, Prévo makes the certificate again at startup, and there is nothing to redo on the phones (still reserve a fixed address in the router: the labels carry the address).

The illustrations on the page and in the two screenshots that follow are diagrams; they will be replaced by real screenshots after testing on an Android phone and an iPhone.

For the IT administrator. The certificate and its key are in donnees\acces\certificat.pem and cle.pem, the local authority in donnees\acces\autorite (rootCA.pem, which the door serves under the name prevo-ca.crt). You can instead supply your own certificate (two PEM files: the “Certificate” step of the assistant, or the options --certificat and --cle): phones then have nothing to recognise; or leave https to the company’s reverse proxy (docs/INSTALLATION.md). Never hand out the file rootCA-key.pem: with it, someone could make certificates that your devices would believe. Prévo neither reads nor serves it.

8.4 On an Android phone

These are the steps of the “Trust the workshop PC” page, as the phone shows them:

  1. Download the certificate (button on the page), then, at the top of the screen, “Download complete”.
  2. Open Settings, then “Security & privacy” (on some phones: “Security” or “Biometrics and security”).
  3. Tap “Encryption & credentials”, often under “More security & privacy” or “Other security settings”. If in doubt, search for “certificate” in the Settings search: the path varies by manufacturer.
  4. Tap “Install a certificate”, then “CA certificate”.
  5. Tap “Install anyway”: Android warns that the network could be monitored. This is normal for a certificate that you install yourself, the workshop PC’s.
  6. Choose the file prevo-ca.crt, in “Downloads”. Android confirms: “CA certificate installed”.
  7. Come back to the Prévo page and tap Try again: Prévo opens on the requested page, and the Dictate button appears in “Report a problem”.

Firefox on Android has its own certificate store and ignores the phone’s: open Prévo with Chrome or the browser supplied with the phone. To stay on Firefox, the page explains the setting to turn on (“Use third party CA certificates”).

8.5 On an iPhone

  1. Download the certificate (button on the page). Safari asks “This website is trying to download a configuration profile”: tap “Allow”, then “Close”.
  2. Open Settings, then “Profile Downloaded”, at the top of Settings (if it is not there: General, “VPN & Device Management”).
  3. Tap “Install” at the top right: the iPhone asks for its passcode, then “Install” a second time, then “Done”.
  4. Open Settings, General, then “About”.
  5. At the very bottom, “Certificate Trust Settings”: turn on the certificate, then “Continue”. This is the step people forget: without it, Safari still refuses the workshop PC.
  6. Go back to Safari and tap Try again: Prévo opens on the requested page.

8.6 Away from the workshop with Tailscale

To look at or close a WO from home or on the move, Prévo goes through a private network: Tailscale links the server PC and your phones to one another, encrypted, without opening anything on the router. Prévo never opens your router to the internet. The IT administrator may prefer the company VPN, which plays the same role.

  1. Create a Tailscale account (there is a free plan; check its terms) and install the Tailscale app on the server PC from its official website, https://tailscale.com/download, then sign in. Prévo does not install it for you: the assistant only shows the link.
  2. In the assistant, “Away from the workshop” step, click I have installed Tailscale and I am signed in. Prévo detects the PC’s name on the private network (in the form pc-atelier.tail1234.ts.net), adds it to its accepted names and asks Tailscale to carry the https for it (tailscale serve). On Windows, one click also turns on the “unattended” mode (unattended), so that Tailscale runs even when nobody is signed in on the PC.
  3. Install the Tailscale app on each phone that leaves the workshop, with the same account, and leave it switched on. Prévo then answers at the https address of the Tailscale name, written on the access record; the phone has no certificate to recognise.
  4. Two reminders, which the assistant displays: turn off key expiry for the server PC in the Tailscale console (Machines › this PC › Disable key expiry), otherwise, after a few months, phones can no longer reach Prévo; and prevent the PC from sleeping (8.7): a PC asleep does not respond, Tailscale or not.

What Prévo never does: open a port on the router, install Tailscale or sign in to it for you, send anything to Tailscale. It only reads the status of the app on the server PC. The manager’s home page warns if Tailscale is disconnected or if the key expires within 14 days, and the sign-in log records the Tailscale account that opened each session coming from outside.

8.7 Prévo starts with the PC

A phone that scans a label at 7 a.m. must not land on “server unreachable”. The assistant (“Startup” step) installs a Windows scheduled task, named Prevo, which starts Prévo 30 seconds after the PC boots, even before anyone has signed in, with no window at all. In the same administrator prompt (only one, announced beforehand), it adds the firewall rule (2.6), has Windows recognise the workshop certificate and, if you asked for it, prevents the PC from sleeping when on mains power (the screen still turns off).

  • With no window, the server writes what it is doing to donnees\journal-serveur.log.
  • The scripts are written to the Prévo folder before they are run (Installer_demarrage.ps1, Retirer_demarrage.ps1): you can read them. If the administrator prompt is refused, nothing is installed, and Prévo offers the fallback “at sign-in” (a task without administrator rights) or the black window to start by hand.
  • Removing it: Settings › Access and installation, or Retirer_demarrage.ps1 (right-click, “Run with PowerShell”, as administrator): the task and the firewall rule are removed, and sleep is put back as it was.
  • On Linux, the assistant gives a systemd service (prevo.service) and the commands to run; on Mac, a launch agent.

8.8 Solo mode

Are you the only one doing maintenance? Solo mode is the manager profile with a lighter menu, not a fourth role. The assistant turns it on for “Just me”; otherwise: Settings, “Solo mode” card (Switch to Solo mode, Leave Solo mode: nothing is deleted).

  • The technician “me”: your technician record, created with your name and pre-filled on each WO. Time spent and authorisations are entered as for any other technician.
  • Lighter menu: Team and Planning move under “More”; on the home page, New WO comes first, then “Report a problem”; on an equipment record, Create a WO comes first.
  • A WO from the label: scan the machine’s QR label (phone, or Prévo’s scan), the record opens, Create a WO: the machine is already filled in.
  • One-step closure: on a WO, the Close button asks in a single window for the end date, the time spent, a part issued from the stores (optional), the failure codes, the job report, the tip and the return to service: technical and administrative closure are done at once (two log lines, and the WO enters the wiki queue). The “one-step closure” setting (Settings, Work orders) remains available outside Solo mode.

8.9 Your data and the GDPR

Prévo handles personal data: names of technicians and requesters, accounts, the sign-in log, the texts of requests and job reports. Here is where it is and who has access to it, for your record of processing activities.

  • Where. On the server PC, in the donnees folder (CSV files, documents, backups) and in donnees\acces (accounts, sessions, sign-in log). Nothing with the publisher, nothing with SELECTIS, nothing online, except the backup copy folder that you choose yourself (USB stick, NAS, synced folder).
  • Passwords. Never in clear: only a fingerprint (scrypt, with a salt) is kept, never shown again. Prévo sends no email; resetting is done on the server PC (8.1).
  • Who has access. Each role reads the tables for its screens (chapter 3): a requester sees neither costs, nor technicians, nor work orders; a technician sees neither the hourly rate nor prices. The manager manages accounts and only the manager reads the sign-in log.
  • Sign-in log (journal-acces.csv): date, account, address, browser, result (sign-in, failure, lockout, sign-out, invitation, revocation…). It is kept for 12 months: older rows are erased. The change log (journal.csv) records who changed what, with no time limit: it is the maintenance history.
  • Right of access, export. Everything is in CSV files readable in Excel; “Export as ZIP” (Settings) gives the 27 files and the documents, “Export (CSV)” (Team › Access) the sign-in log. A deactivated account stays in the list (for the history) but cannot sign in.
  • The AI assistant. Off by default. Provider: the one the manager sets on the server PC: Ollama on the workshop PC (nothing leaves the workshop), or an online service, which they must allow explicitly. Country: that of the chosen provider; read its terms before allowing it, the “AI: data sent to …” note reminds you of this permanently (5.8). What is sent: only what the function needs (5.3); telephone numbers and email addresses found in a text are replaced by “[téléphone]” and “[courriel]” before sending; never the names of technicians and requesters, hourly rates, costs, documents or photos; a name written in a job report is sent with the text. Who decides: the manager, on the server PC, never a workstation; the IT administrator follows the company’s policy on employee data.
  • Dictation sends the voice to Google or Microsoft (chapter 6), workstation by workstation, with a warning the first time it is used.
  • New versions: once a day, on the manager’s workstation, Prévo reads a public file on prevo.pro, with no username, installation number or statistics; prevo.pro sees, as with any visit, the workshop’s public internet address, the browser and Prévo’s local address. It can be turned off in Settings (2.9). This is the only connection that Prévo opens by itself to the internet.

8.10 The company directory

Prévo does not connect to the company directory (Active Directory, LDAP, Entra ID, Google Workspace): no single sign-on, no synchronisation of accounts. This is a choice: Prévo fits in a single Python file and has to stay installable by a workshop without an IT administrator. What does exist:

  • local accounts, created by the manager or by the IT administrator (one per employee, requesters included if you set it up that way);
  • the export of the sign-in log, for your own monitoring;
  • the reverse proxy and the company VPN, to put Prévo behind your own access controls (docs/INSTALLATION.md).
