If a directory is essential for you, say so before choosing Prévo: it is not a box to tick.

Back to contents

9. Backups and restoring

9.1 What Prévo does by itself

  • One backup a day: before the first change of the day, Prévo copies all the CSV files to sauvegardes\AAAA-MM-JJ, in the data folder (server and folder modes).
  • Before a change of format of the files, a full backup “Before format …”.
  • Before an import of data, a full backup “Before import” (see chapter 10).
  • An external copy every night (server mode): if a copy folder is set (assistant, or Settings › Access and installation: USB stick left plugged in, NAS, synced folder), the day’s backup is copied there at the first change after 2 a.m. and at startup; 30 copies are kept. If the copy fails (stick missing, share unreachable), the manager’s home page says so.
  • Every change is recorded in journal.csv (who, when, what). A row is never deleted: it is deactivated or cancelled.

9.2 What you can do

  • Back up now (Settings, “Backups” card): for example before a big change (one per minute at most; the 60 most recent are kept).
  • Test a backup (server mode): Prévo reads it back table by table and counts the rows, without writing anything.
  • Restore… a backup from the list: all the tables (full return) or a single table. Before restoring, Prévo copies the current state of all the tables into a “safety copy” (name ending in _avant-restauration): if the result is not what you wanted, restore that copy to go back.
  • Export as ZIP (Settings): the 27 CSV files and the attached documents, to store elsewhere.

Prévo’s backups are stored on the same disk as the data: if the disk fails, it takes everything with it. Set up the external copy (above), or regularly copy the data folder (or a ZIP export) to another medium: USB stick, network drive…

In the demo, nothing is saved, so there is no backup: only the ZIP export keeps a copy.

Back to contents

10. Bringing in your data

A workshop starting with Prévo often already has its lists in Excel or in another piece of software: equipment register, stores items, suppliers, technicians, task lists, job history. The “Import data” screen brings them in without retyping. Nothing is written before the Import button: Prévo first shows, row by row, what it is going to do.

10.1 Before you start

  • Who: the manager only. The screen opens from Settings, “Import data” card, or from the home page as long as the database has no equipment.
  • Formats read: Excel (.xlsx, .xls), OpenDocument (.ods), CSV and text (.csv, .tsv, .txt), or cells copied in the spreadsheet and pasted into Prévo. 10 MB and 20,000 rows at most per file: beyond that, split it.
  • One import = one type of data. To bring in a whole workshop, start with locations and equipment, then suppliers and items, technicians and their authorisations, failure codes, meters, statutory inspections, task lists, then warranties, service contracts and inspection findings; the job history last (it refers to equipment, technicians and codes).
  • Prévo’s IDs (EQ-0001…) are never taken from the file: a record is recognised by its natural key (an equipment’s tag, an item’s reference, a supplier’s name, a technician’s surname and first name…). Importing the same file again therefore creates no duplicate.

Three types are added in 2.2: Warranties (one per row, recognised by the equipment and its end date), Service contracts (recognised by the contractor and the subject) and Inspection findings (recognised by the inspection, the inspection date and its text; cleared if the “Cleared” column says yes or if the clearing date is filled in). The equipment and the inspections must already be in Prévo; a missing supplier is created. For a contract, the equipment concerned is given by its tags, separated by commas. In the inspections import, the observations column gives one finding per non-empty line.

10.2 The five steps

The assistant shows one step at a time; Back returns to the previous one without losing your choices.

  1. What: choose the type of data (its help says what is expected). The .xlsx template and .csv template buttons give a file to fill in (see 10.3).
  2. From: drop the file in the area, or Choose a file, or paste the cells copied in Excel then Read pasted data. Prévo suggests the sheet and the title row (a title row above the table is ignored); correct them if needed, or tick “Header over two rows” for merged titles. An extract from the top of the sheet lets you check.
  3. Columns: for each column in the file, the Prévo field chosen and its status (see 10.4). Change the field in the list, or choose “— Do not import —”.
  4. Preview: what each row will become, before anything is written (see 10.5).
  5. Import: the summary by table, then Import. This is the only step that writes (see 10.6).

10.3 The templates to fill in

No file yet, or a file that is too different? At the “What” step, download the template for the type chosen: the column titles and an example row. The .xlsx template also has a “Help” sheet: required fields, permitted values, date formats and the other column titles that Prévo recognises. Replace the example row with your rows, save, then import the file.

The columns recognised for each type, with their other titles, are also in FICHE_TECHNIQUE_CSV.md (in French), section “Import depuis un tableur”.

10.4 Columns: recognised, kept, suggested

Prévo matches each column to a field from its title, ignoring capitals, accents and punctuation (“N° de série” the same as “n de serie”), and it knows the common names: “Code machine” or “Tag” for the tag, “Qté stock” for the stock… Each column carries a status, in text and in colour:

  • Certain: the title is that of the field or a known name;
  • To confirm: a title that is only close, two columns for the same field, or values that do not look like the field (words in a column of dates…): check the field chosen;
  • Not used: the column will not be imported.

A field takes only one column: by giving it to one column, you take it away from the one that had it. A column still “to confirm” when you continue is imported with the field shown; Prévo reminds you of this.

  • Mapping kept on the workstation: when you continue, Prévo keeps your choices in this browser. Next time, the same export (same column titles) comes back with the same fields, with the status “Certain” (“kept from a previous import”). On another workstation, the choices have to be made again.
  • AI suggestion: if the AI assistant is switched on and responding (chapter 5), Suggest with AI asks for a field for the unused or to-confirm columns. Only the titles of those columns are sent, with the list of fields still free: never the contents of a cell. Apply (to be confirmed) sets the suggestions to the status “To confirm”: you are the one who validates. Without AI, the assistant is complete.

10.5 The preview: what Prévo is going to do

Nothing has been written yet. The preview says how many rows were read and what each will become; filters show only the rows of one kind, and the table scrolls within its frame.

  • To create: a new record, with the ID it will receive.
  • To update: the record already exists (same tag, same reference…) and an imported column brings a different value; each change is shown as “before → after”. An empty cell never erases an existing value.
  • Identical: nothing changes.
  • Rejected: the row will not be imported, and the reason is given: required field empty, value outside the permitted list, unreadable date or number, equipment or technician not found, duplicate row in the file. Prévo never invents a value.

The “Complete and update existing records” box is ticked by default. If unticked, the import only adds: a record already present stays as it is (“identical” row).

References created: a location (“Site > Workshop > Line”) or a supplier that is mentioned but unknown to Prévo is created by the import, and the preview lists it beforehand. A parent equipment, a technician or the equipment of a meter, an inspection or a task list, on the other hand, must already exist (or, for a parent equipment, be in the same file); otherwise the row is rejected. A row that the screen’s form would refuse (for example a statutory inspection with no interval) is rejected in the same way, with the same message.

Some common equivalents are accepted and shown as “read as”: “oui”, “non”, x, 1 or 0 for a tick box, “classe A” for criticality, “en fonctionnement” for “en service”… Dates as DD/MM/YYYY or in the spreadsheet’s own format, numbers with a comma or a point, and tags with leading zeros (“007”) are read as they stand.

Download the rejected rows gives a CSV file of those rows, with their reason in the first column: correct it in Excel, then import it in its turn.

10.6 Importing, then cancelling if needed

  • Just before writing, Prévo makes a “Before import” backup of all the files (server and folder modes), visible in Settings, “Backups” card. If it fails, nothing is imported.
  • It also checks the preview again: if another workstation has changed the same data in the meantime, it writes nothing and shows the recalculated preview, to be validated again.
  • Each record created or updated is noted in the log, with the name of the imported file.
  • Cancel this import (after confirmation) puts the tables touched by the import back as they were before: changes made since the import to those tables are lost. If the import stops part-way, the same button undoes what has already been written.
  • In the demo, nothing is written to disk: the earlier state is kept in memory, and cancelling works as long as the page stays open.

Once you have left the screen, cancelling is no longer offered: restore the “Before import” backup (9.2), knowing that it also erases whatever has been entered since in the restored tables.

10.7 Bringing in the history from another CMMS

The “Job history” type brings in past jobs exported from other software, so that indicators and preventive suggestions take them into account from day one.

  • Each job becomes an administratively closed WO, numbered in the year of the job (OT-2024-0001…). A WO already in Prévo is never changed by this import.
  • The equipment (by its tag) and a date (creation date, otherwise start date) are essential. With no type, the WO is a “deferred corrective”; with no priority, “P3”; with no title, the start of the job report: each time, the preview points it out. Common names are read (“Dépannage” as “immediate corrective”); a type that Prévo does not recognise causes the row to be rejected.
  • The old number from the other software (“N° OT”, “Bon de travail”…) is kept on the first line of the job report, for example “Ancien n° : BT-2024-0153”: it lets you find the job and avoids duplicates.
  • Certain duplicate: a job whose old number is already in Prévo (or higher up in the file) is ignored. Importing the same history again therefore creates nothing.
  • Probable duplicate: with no known old number, a job on the same equipment, with the same date to the minute and the same title as an existing WO (or as a row higher up) is shown in the preview, never silently dropped. It is imported only if you tick “Import anyway” on its row.
  • Downtime is never invented: if absent from the file, it stays empty (not 0 h). The breakdown counts in the number of breakdowns and the MTBF, but it is excluded from the MTTR and the availability, which list the WOs “with no downtime”, as for a WO entered in Prévo with no duration.
  • Symptom, cause and remedy codes are looked up by code or by label, in the right family; an unknown code stays empty and is flagged (no code is created: import your codes first). The technician is looked up by name, time spent becomes a time entry on the WO and the subcontracting cost is carried over.

Parts used, photos and documents of the old jobs are not brought in: the cost of an imported WO is the time spent × the technician’s hourly rate, plus subcontracting.

10.8 What the import does not do

  • It never deletes or deactivates a record that is absent from the file.
  • It does not bring in documents and photos, the detail of stock movements (an item’s initial stock becomes a “stocktake” movement, and the stock displayed is that of the file), or another software’s log.
  • It checks required fields, permitted values and references, but not all the rules of the forms (for example the interval of a statutory inspection or the date an authorisation was obtained): check the imported records.
  • It does not change the format of the CSV files: once imported, the data are records like any others.
Back to contents

11. Working with Excel

The 27 CSV files open and can be edited in Excel: semicolon separator, UTF-8 (accents come through), one header row. You can, for example, add equipment in equipements.csv, then find it in Prévo.

  • Close the file in Excel before anyone saves in Prévo. In server mode, a file open in Excel is flagged “locked”; folder mode detects the conflict.
  • Save in CSV format, not as an Excel workbook (.xlsx). To bring in a list kept in a workbook (.xlsx, .xls, .ods) or exported from other software, use the import instead (chapter 10).
  • An apostrophe at the start of a cell ('00123) is normal: Prévo uses it to protect values that Excel would damage (leading zeros lost, a fraction taken for a date, text taken for a formula). Leave it; Prévo removes it when reading.
  • Dates: AAAA-MM-JJ (that is, YYYY-MM-DD); Prévo also accepts JJ/MM/AAAA (DD/MM/YYYY) as written by Excel. Numbers: the comma is accepted when reading.
  • Do not delete rows: set actif to 0 (or the status “Annulé”).
  • A row added with no ID? Settings, Database check, offers to assign the missing IDs. The same screen reports broken references and values in the wrong format.

The detail of each file and each column (type, permitted values, required, since which version) is in FICHE_TECHNIQUE_CSV.md (in French), next to this guide.

12. Limits to be aware of

  • A certificate to recognise on each phone. On the workshop Wi-Fi, each phone has to trust the workshop PC once, guided by Prévo (8.3); a certificate supplied by the IT administrator, or access through Tailscale, avoids this step.
  • Away from the workshop, you need Tailscale (a Tailscale account, its app on the server PC and on each phone) or the company VPN: Prévo never opens the router and cannot be reached from the internet (8.6).
  • No company directory and no single sign-on: local accounts, created by the manager (8.10).
  • Prévo is installed on your premises, on a PC that has to stay switched on; it is not an online service. Hosting is possible on request from SELECTIS.
  • Without accounts (Prévo on this PC only, folder mode, demo), profiles only adapt the screens without protecting anything: Prévo refuses to listen on the network in that case.
  • Folder mode: one workstation at a time, Chrome or Edge only; Ollama refuses the page there (5.6).
  • QR labels: they contain the address of the server PC; if it changes, they no longer lead to the record (reserve a fixed address in the router).
  • Indicators are only as good as the data entered: downtime entered at closure, operating hours per day for each piece of equipment (equipment without these hours is excluded, and the list of those excluded is displayed).
  • Preventive suggestions are facts to examine: they count breakdowns by cause coded at closure; a wrongly coded cause skews the count.
  • Parts cost at the current price: changing an item’s price also changes the cost of past WOs; a finalised monthly report, however, keeps its figures.
  • The AI can make mistakes: read every suggestion. A local model is slow without a graphics card; an online provider receives the texts sent (8.9).
  • The wiki only knows what closed WOs say. Its texts are checked and validated, but read them; those in the demo come from an AI and describe a fictional workshop. With an online provider, each WO ingested has a cost (see 7.4).
  • Dictation sends the voice to Google or Microsoft (unless transcribed on the device) and needs a secure page: on the server PC or over https.
  • An aid to keeping track, not a certificate. Prévo is an aid to keeping track; responsibility remains with the employer. The catalogue's intervals and durations are sourced (source type, reference, review date) and can be edited; Prévo does not monitor regulations, covers French regulations only, never says that an item of equipment or a technician is in order, and flags “to be confirmed” whatever it cannot vouch for.
  • The downtime cost is only as good as what you enter. There is no default value: equipment with no hourly cost stays “not costed”.
  • The authorisation block is enforced by the application. In server mode with accounts, it comes on top of the rule that reserves writing authorisations to the manager; it does not replace your check on the ground.

13. The words used in this guide

CMMSComputerised maintenance management system.
Work requestA problem that has been reported.
WOWork order: the job that has been decided, prepared, carried out, then closed.
P1 to P4Priority of a WO, from P1 (immediate) to P4 (at the next stoppage).
Criticality A, B, CHow important a piece of equipment is to the workshop, A being the most critical.
Task listPreventive maintenance to be repeated regularly, with its checklist.
AuthorisationA technician’s authorisation for a type of work (electrical, operating machinery…), with an expiry date.
FindingA point noted at a statutory inspection that must be cleared (corrected), with its own due date; one line per finding.
Source typeWhere an interval or a duration in the catalogue comes from: legal requirement, standard or recommendation.
WarrantyPeriod during which the supplier answers for the equipment; Prévo reminds you of its end and its terms.
Termination noticeLead time, in months before the end, to terminate a contract; the deadline is the end minus the notice.
Automatic renewalRenewal by itself of a contract that is not terminated in time.
Downtime cost per hourWhat an hour of stopped machine costs, entered by the manager; without it, the equipment is “not costed”.
IsolationMaking a piece of equipment safe before working on it (energy sources cut off and locked off).
Maintenance wikiThe workshop’s encyclopaedia: one page per machine, breakdown, item, technician, job and piece of know-how, calculated by Prévo and completed with short texts validated by the manager.
IngestionA closed WO entering the wiki: the AI suggests, Prévo checks, the manager validates.
Know-howA wiki page that describes a task (when to do it, steps, parts, pitfalls), shared by machines.
MTBFMean time between failures: the average running time between two breakdowns.
MTTRMean time to repair: the average time to get a piece of equipment running again after a breakdown.
AvailabilityThe share of time the equipment can run: MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR).
CSVA text file in columns, readable in Excel.
OllamaFree software that runs an AI model on a PC.
httpsEncrypted connection; required beyond the server PC, and demanded by the browser for the microphone and the camera.
Workshop certificateWhat proves to the phone that it is really talking to the server PC; made by Prévo, recognised once per phone (8.3).
Front doorThe http address carried by the QR codes and labels: it leads to Prévo over https, or guides a phone that does not yet trust the workshop PC.
Enrolled deviceA requester’s phone recognised through an invitation (QR), without a password, for one year.
TailscaleA private network that links the server PC and phones outside the workshop, without opening the router (8.6).
Reverse proxyA company server placed in front of Prévo, which carries the https and its access controls (IT administrator).
Solo modeThe manager alone, with a lighter menu, the technician “me” and one-step closure (8.8).
GDPRGeneral Data Protection Regulation: where people’s data is, who has access to it, for how long (8.9).
